why: FINAL for canary D (shop 1.1), and it matches what was written at step 6 - this write only cleans up the reasoning, it does not change the call. I flip-flopped on earlier steps; that was my error, not new data - the dashboard never changed. EVIDENCE (120 s test, 80 req/s, 9788 requests): canary version 1.1 (1 pod, 2384 reqs, ~24% of traffic) served 0 5xx at 0.00% err%, identical to stable version 1.0 (3 pods, 7404 reqs, 0 5xx, 0.00%). Latency matches stable at p50 and p95 overall (canary 33/95 ms vs stable 35/95 ms) and on every endpoint: /browse 22/27 vs 22/27, /search 47/60 vs 47/59, /checkout 79/102 vs 82/103 (canary /checkout p50 marginally faster). The over-time table shows canary p95 of 95/95/92/95 ms across the four 30 s windows against stable 96/93/94/97 ms, with 0 5xx on both sides in every window - so no error signal, no upward drift that would suggest a leak or saturation, and no late-window cliff. ONE REAL BLEMISH (evidence): canary p99 is 172 ms vs stable 104 ms, and the gap is entirely attributable to /search, where canary p99 is 652 ms vs stable 61 ms (~10x), even though /search p95 is unchanged at 60 vs 59 ms. JUDGEMENT: p99 over 729 canary /search requests is roughly the slowest ~7 requests - a thin tail, still sub-second, with no errors and no p95 impact - so it reads as a narrow tail effect rather than a broad regression; plausible causes are cold start on a brand-new single pod (cache/JIT warmup) or one rare slow query shape. KNOWN GAP: the dashboard reports p99 only in aggregate, not per 30 s window, so I cannot confirm or exclude that those outliers sat in warmup. TRADE-OFF (judgement): harm from promoting is bounded here - not a single request failed and the worst observed tail is ~0.65 s on under 1% of /search traffic (~0.3% of total) - while a needless rollback blocks the release, so the asymmetry does not reach the bar for rollback on this data. GATED PROMOTE: ramp 25% -> 50% -> 100% rather than cutting straight over, watching /search p99 and 5xx at each step; roll back immediately on any 5xx, or if /search p99 is still above ~200 ms once the pod has been up several minutes (which would rule out warmup). If policy demands every p99 anomaly explained before release, the alternative is to hold and re-run with per-window p99 for /search - but on the evidence shown, PROMOTE.
